title: Find Probability from Tables: Favorable over Total
description: Use Total first, read SAT-style given conditions as restrictions, and find Favorable outcomes within the correct table group.

questions.stem_html: The table gives the number of students by club and primary way of getting to school. Each student appears once. A student is selected at random from the whole table. What is the probability that the student bikes? Give the exact value as a fraction or terminating decimal if possible.
questions.explanation_html: First count the 67 students in the allowed selection group. Of those, 12 meet the requested condition. The probability is \(\frac{12}{67}\).
questions.variation: Use the entire group for an unconditional or joint probability

questions.stem_html: The table gives the number of students by club and primary way of getting to school. Each student appears once. An Art student is selected at random. What is the probability that this student takes the bus? Give the exact value as a fraction or terminating decimal if possible.
questions.explanation_html: First count the 44 students in the allowed selection group. Of those, 14 meet the requested condition. The probability is \(\frac{7}{22}\).

questions.stem_html: The table gives the number of students by club and primary way of getting to school. Each student appears once. A student is selected at random from those who take the bus or bike. What is the probability that this student is in Art? Give the exact value as a fraction or terminating decimal if possible.
questions.explanation_html: First count the 53 students in the allowed selection group. Of those, 19 meet the requested condition. The probability is \(\frac{19}{53}\).
questions.variation: Combine several permitted categories before counting favorable cases

questions.stem_html: The entries count students, each in one club and one travel group. For a randomly selected Art student, the probability of biking is \(\frac{1}{3}\). What is x?
questions.explanation_html: The Art total is 24 + x. Set x divided by that total equal to \(\frac{1}{3}\). Solving gives x = 12.
questions.variation: Use a conditional probability to recover a missing count
